body_markdown:
The debut of the Ford Mustang at the 1964 New York World’s Fair is a well-known tale by now. The event, which drew thousands and thousands of spectators to tour booths and displays that invited them to “step into the future,” was the perfect cocktail of enthusiasm, optimism, and curiosity to launch what would become Ford’s most iconic nameplate. But did you know that Disney was instrumental in the success of the Mustang launch?


1965 Ford Mustang fastback in front of the Ford Pavilion at the 1964 World’s Fair in New York.


Ford


A new film produced by the Hagerty Driver’s Foundation recounts the backstory behind the confluence of genius between Ford, Disney, and the moment at hand back in ’64. In the video, historians such as Ted Ryan, the archive and brand manager for[Ford Motor Company](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/the-ford-vault-is-filled-with-concepts-mules-and-milestones/) , recount what made the launch of the Mustang so special. The crux: The Mustang’s launch was *different* .


Preston Rose / Hagerty Drivers Foundation


“There’s been no other introduction of a car like that before, or sadly after that date,” remarks the familiar voice of Tom Cotter, our *Barn Find Hunter* . “You could write a Harvard Business School study about that introduction.”


At the ’64 World’s Fair, Ford built a massive structure that it called the “Ford Pavilion.” Part of that pavilion was something called the “Magic Skyway,” which was essentially a theme park ride you’d enjoy from the seat of a new Ford, Lincoln, or Mercury vehicle. Ford enlisted the help of the inimitable Walt Disney to help it design the Pavilion and the Magic Skyway.


Preston Rose / Hagerty Drivers Foundation


“Walt \[Disney\] was really interested in urban planning,” said Becky Cline, director of the Walt Disney Archives. “He was also interested in how to use technology to improve people’s lives.” The ensuing collaboration between two juggernauts of American industry and entertainment remains one of the all-time greats.


Between the brilliance of the Magic Skyway and the all-out[media stampede](https://www.hagerty.com/media/automotive-history/the-early-mustangs-media-stampede/) that Ford launched to drum up enthusiasm for the[Mustang](https://www.hagerty.com/media/buying-and-selling/auctions/from-dinos-to-space-city-this-65-new-york-worlds-fair-mustang-saw-it-all/) , the car essentially became an instant classic—and only further cemented that title as time went on.


[Nathan Petroelje](https://www.hagerty.com/media/author/nathan-petroelje/)


Naturally, that’s what made the[World’s Fair Mustang](https://driversfoundation.org/registry/1965-ford-mustang-new-york-worlds-fair-magic-skyway) such an important candidate for the[National Historic Vehicle Register](https://driversfoundation.org/register#cars) , the only federally recognized program that records and preserves the history of America’s most significant automobiles. The car was[added to the register](https://www.hagerty.com/media/car-profiles/1965-magic-skyway-mustang-added-to-national-historic-vehicle-register/) in July of this year.


Be sure to watch the entire film, which we’ve embedded below. Even the most hardcore Mustang fans are likely to learn something new.
